short_answer: Kelso Sturgeon is a real, long running name in pick selling and betting books. His bio on Don Best and on an archived Vegas Sports Masters page gives a long list of credentials, a Las Vegas home and a phone number. In that sense he is a real seller, not an invented persona.

On 16 Nov 2026 we could not find a working place to buy his picks. The Vegas Sports Masters site he sold through no longer loads, its .com domain goes to a domain sale page, and the old kelsosportshandicapping.com address showed unrelated content in a 2026 archive copy. A Swedish betting blog sits on kelsosturgeon.com; we saw nothing linking it to him.

We found no full record of his picks. Buyer posts on HandicappingReviews.org and Pregame.com from 2009 to 2022 lean clearly negative, with repeated complaints about losing runs, upsell calls and refunds, and a few buyers who said he won for them. Treat any current offer under his name with care and ask for a complete record first.
pricing_intro: We found no live seller price on 16 Nov 2026. The archived Vegas Sports Masters shop page from Dec 2022 showed no products in the copy we opened. The only prices we saw are on an undated third party review, so treat them as history, not a current offer.
pricing: Third party listing, undated; not a verified current offer
About $200 to $300 per sport per season
guarantee: We found no guarantee wording from the seller. The archived 2023 Vegas Sports Masters page links to a refund and privacy policy, but we did not open a copy of it, so we make no claim about its terms.

Two buyers describe what happened when things went wrong. One wrote in 2016 that the service sent him the wrong games, admitted the mistake and offered only extra games. Another wrote in 2019 that he asked for a refund and got no reply. These are single, unverified accounts.

claims_note: Most claims are about his career, not his picks. A long career in the betting world does not show that his picks beat the closing line or the vig.

The banner wins are picked by the seller. Forum members wrote in 2011 that he promoted winning big unit plays and said little about losing ones. That is one reading of his marketing, not a measured fact.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Kelso Sturgeon pick, and no court or regulator record about the service.

What the seller published: banner results such as a 100 unit Falcons win and a Monday night sweep on the archived 2023 page. A 2009 Pregame thread also quotes an 11 and 0 run on his top college basketball plays. These are chosen runs, not a record.

Buyers posted their own partial results. A 2019 buyer posted a full March Madness card that he said went 0 and 7 on one day, and a 2017 reviewer listed eight college basketball losses in a row. These are partial and unverified.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Kelso Sturgeon is mostly on one review site and two forum threads, and none of it is newer than 2022. Below is what we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We read 13 buyer comments on HandicappingReviews.org dated 2013 to 2022 and two Pregame forum threads from 2009, 2011 and 2019. About ten of the buyer comments are negative. The same complaints repeat across years: long losing runs, big unit plays that lost, constant calls to upgrade, and refunds that did not come. One 2019 complaint appears on both sites with the same pick list, so it is likely one buyer. On the positive side, one 2013 buyer said he did his homework and won for him, a 2014 buyer broke even in two weeks, and a 2011 forum member called him a long term winner. One other said he made money years earlier but not lately. We found nothing newer than 2022.
A reviewer on HandicappingReviews.org wrote that the picks cost him a lot of money before he decided they were a waste of time, and that only the seller was making money.

A Pregame member posted the college basketball card he bought for the NCAA tournament and said it went 0 for 7 on Saturday after losing 55 units on Friday. He said he asked for a refund and got no reply. The same pick list was posted as a review on HandicappingReviews.org the next day. Other members replied that he had been selling picks for decades and told the buyer to stop.

A reviewer said he lost eight college basketball games over three days of the 2017 tournament and listed the teams. Two more 2017 reviews on the same page called the picks very poor without giving results.

A buyer of a November football package said he quit after starting 3 and 5. He wrote that he was once sent the wrong games, that the service admitted the error later, and that it offered only extra games, not money.

A reviewer said the picks made him money a few years earlier but had been disappointing since. He complained that "he never shows his losses" on the website and that large unit plays were sold as near locks.
A family wrote that the service kept mailing promotions to a relative who had died almost a year earlier and that they could not reach anyone to stop it. This is about marketing, not picks.
A buyer said the service kept pushing upgrades before his current package had run out and that he would not sign up again.
A buyer two weeks into a package said he had broken even both weeks and that the site and service were decent.
A reviewer said the picks can look unusual, often underdogs, but that the handicapper does his homework and had led him to wins.

A Pregame member wrote that he used the NFL, NBA and baseball picks for over a year and lost thousands of dollars. He alleged constant sales calls and a dispute over a refund he said he was owed. We could not verify any of it.
In the same thread another member defended him as a long term winner, said every capper has losing streaks, and said he used to get useful free mailers from him.

A third member advised following him only on hot streaks and bigger plays, and said he talked about winners while skipping losers, citing two big unit losses in one week of which only one was mentioned.

A Better Business Bureau search for Kelso Sturgeon in Las Vegas returned no results. On Reddit, the only post naming him we found was a 2017 question about a betting book he co wrote with Jim Feist, with no buyer reports. Our web searches found no SBR, TheRX or Covers thread with buyer results.

conflicts: Several web addresses tied to his name no longer belong to his business as far as we can tell. kelsosturgeon.com is a Swedish betting and casino blog, kelsosportshandicapping.com showed unrelated content in an April 2026 archive copy, and vegassportsmasters.com redirected to a domain sale page. A buyer should not assume any of these speak for him.
The archived Vegas Sports Masters page also sold picks from other handicappers, including Jim Feist and Jim Hurley, so it was a storefront for several names, not his alone.
strengths: A real, named person with a long public career, books, and a Las Vegas phone number on his old sales page.
His bio is detailed and specific, which makes the career claims checkable in principle.
Some buyers over the years said he won for them or that he did real homework.
concerns: No working sales site, prices or terms from the seller on 16 Nov 2026.
No full public record. Every result we saw was chosen by the seller or posted by a single buyer.
Buyer posts from 2011 to 2022 repeat the same complaints: losing runs, upsell calls and refunds not paid.
Old domains under his name now show unrelated sites, which makes it easy to confuse a copycat with the real service.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Confirm you are dealing with the real seller. Several old domains under his name now show other content.
Get refund or guarantee terms in writing before you pay. Most guarantees in this business are credits, not cash.
Count units, not wins. Big unit plays that lose can wipe out many small winners.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: He is a real person with a long career in betting media and pick selling, and his bio gives a Las Vegas phone number. We could not verify that his picks win over time, we found no working sales site on 16 Nov 2026, and buyer posts from 2009 to 2022 are mostly negative. We found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Kelso Sturgeon cost?
We found no current price from the seller. An undated third party review lists daily picks at $25 to $75 and a monthly package at $499.
Does Kelso Sturgeon have a verified record?
No. His old sales page showed selected wins such as a 100 unit game of the year. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.
Is Kelso Sturgeon still selling picks?

His Don Best profile is still online, but on 16 Nov 2026 the Vegas Sports Masters site he sold through did not load and its .com domain went to a sale page. The newest buyer review we found is from 2022.
